assignments.brief_reason: Blocking is tied to emotionally inflammatory invective across both sides.
Uses a harm/toxicity threshold based on harshness not conducive to civil conversation.
Mentions impartiality and discourse-quality concerns rather than meaningful pairwise comparison influence.
Targets hateful name-calling as the main removal trigger (toxicity/harm threshold).
Describes a general neutrality/threat-focus approach, not a specific pair-comparison effect.
Treats adult political-news context as mitigating offensiveness, i.e., a language/toxicity line-drawing.
Anger/desire to engage reflects affect but not a clear keeping/removal comparison criterion.
Explicit partisan slurs/insults indicate sensitivity to toxic name-calling.
Keeps all when no hate speech is detected (explicit toxicity threshold).
Primary checks are vulgarity/misinformation rather than the codebook’s harm/toxicity or pair-comparison themes.
Removal is based on expected discussion quality/seriousness rather than substantive pair comparisons.
Claims unbiased moderation based on whether attacks disrupt discussion, not on pair comparisons.
Uncertainty about free speech vs fake news/bullies does not fit the two provided themes cleanly.
Looks for intolerance and group insults framed as entertainment (toxic/harmful language threshold).
Uses threat/violence presence as the decisive harm threshold.
Rudeness without a point is still allowed under free speech—tone-based harm line-drawing.
Downweights expletives; bans focus on hateful/threatening content (toxicity thresholds).
Prioritizes language cues (e.g., cursing) over politics for keeping/removal.
Keeps posts because they’re others’ thoughts worth hearing; not clearly about pairwise comparison influence.
No discernible criterion beyond randomness.
